response:
Confidence is the first requirement because fractional reserve banking works only when depositors believe their money is safe and accessible on demand and therefore keep the bulk of deposits in the bank rather than demanding cash all at once, which allows banks to lend out reserves instead of holding them idle Confidence

Liquidity is the second requirement because a bank holds only a fraction of deposits as reserves so it depends on the ability to obtain additional funds quickly from the interbank market or a central bank lender of last resort when withdrawal demand spikes, preventing a temporary shortfall from becoming an insolvency Liquidity

prompt: The response must start with a verb. Galois theory explained in depth using symbols and equations
response:
Explore Galois theory as the study of field extensions via their automorphisms. Let $F\subseteq E$ be fields.

A field extension $E/F$ has degree $[E:F]=\dim_F E$ and is 
* algebraic if every $\alpha\in E$ satisfies $f(\alpha)=0$ for some $0\neq f\in F[x]$,
* separable if for each $\alpha\in E$, $[F(\alpha):F]=\deg m_{\alpha,F}$ where $m_{\alpha,F}$ is the minimal polynomial,
* normal if every $f\in F[x]$ with a root in $E$ splits completely in $E$.

$E/F$ is Galois iff it is finite, separable and normal. Then

$$\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)=\{\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(E)\mid \sigma|_F=\operatorname{id}_F\}$$

is a finite group under composition and

$$[E:F]=|\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)|.$$

For $\alpha\in E$ the orbit under $G=\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$ is
$\operatorname{Orb}_G(\alpha)=\{\sigma(\alpha):\sigma\in G\}$ and the fixed field is

$$E^G=\{x\in E\mid \sigma(x)=x\ \forall\sigma\in G\},\qquad F^{G}=F.$$

Let $K$ be intermediate $F\subseteq K\subseteq E$. Then
$[E:F]=[E:K][K:F]$ and

$$|\operatorname{Gal}(E/F):\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)|=[K:F],\qquad 
\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)=\{\sigma\in G\mid \sigma|_K=\operatorname{id}_K\}.$$

The Fundamental Theorem:
The map $K\mapsto\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)$ gives a inclusion-reversing bijection

$$\{ \text{intermediate fields }F\subseteq K\subseteq E\}\longleftrightarrow\{\text{subgroups }H\le G\}$$

with $K^{ \operatorname{Gal}(E/K)}=K$ and $\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)^{E}=K$, and $K/F$ is Galois iff $\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)\triangleleft G$, in which case
$\operatorname{Gal}(K/F)\simeq G/\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)$.

For a separable polynomial $f\in F[x]$ let $E$ be its splitting field. Then $E/F$ is Galois and

$$\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)\simeq \{\text{permutations of the roots of }f\}$$

preserving $F$-relations. In particular $\sigma(\alpha_i)=\alpha_{\pi(i)}$.

Example. $f(x)=x^3-2\in\mathbb Q[x]$. Let $\theta=\sqrt[3]{2}$, $\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}$.
Splitting field $E=\mathbb Q(\theta,\omega)$ with $[E:\mathbb Q]=6$.
$G=\operatorname{Gal}(E/\mathbb Q)\simeq S_3$ generated by
$\sigma:\theta\mapsto\omega\theta,\ \omega\mapsto\omega$ and
$\tau:\theta\mapsto\theta,\ \omega\mapsto\omega^2$.
The intermediate fields correspond to the lattice of subgroups:
$\mathbb Q\subset\mathbb Q(\omega)\subset E$, $\mathbb Q\subset\mathbb Q(\theta)\subset E$, $\mathbb Q\subset\mathbb Q(\omega\theta)\subset E$, $\mathbb Q\subset\mathbb Q(\omega^2\theta)\subset E$.

Solvability is expressed as $G$ solvable by abelian extensions, i.e. a chain
$$E=E_0\supset E_1\supset\cdots\supset E_n=F$$
with $\operatorname{Gal}(E_i/E_{i+1})$ abelian, equivalent to $f$ solvable by radicals.

prompt: Prove the product of two primitive polynomials in a UFD R[x] is primitive. Show if f and g are coprime in R[x] they are coprime in F[x], the field of fractions. The response must start with a verb.
response:
Prove that for $f,g\in R[x]$ the content satisfies
$c(fg)=c(f)c(g)$ up to associates.  Put $c(f)=(a_{0},\dots ,a_{n})\subset R$
for $f=\sum a_{i}x^{i}$ and write $\bar{\phantom{a}}$ for reduction mod a
non-zero prime $p\subset R$.  $R/p$ is an integral domain and so is
$(R/p)[x]$.  If $p\mid c(fg)$ then $\bar f\,\bar g=0$ in $(R/p)[x]$.
Hence $\bar f=0$ or $\bar g=0$.  Now $p\mid c(f)$ iff $\bar f=0$, so

\[
p\mid c(fg)\Longrightarrow p\mid c(f)\ \text{or}\ p\mid c(g).
\]

In particular $p\mid c(fg)$ and $f$ primitive, i.e. $\bar f\ne0$, implies
$\bar g=0$, i.e. $p\mid c(g)$.  Hence every prime divisor of $c(fg)$ divides
$c(f)$ or $c(g)$ and

\[
c(fg)=c(f)c(g)\quad\text{up to associates,}
\]

so $c(fg)=1$ whenever $c(f)=c(g)=1$.  If $f$ is primitive then
$c(fh)=c(h)$ for every $h$, whence $f$ primitive $\Rightarrow$ $fg$
primitive iff $g$ primitive.  In particular the product of two primitive
polynomials is primitive.

Now let $d\in F[x]$ divide $f$ and $g$ in $F[x]$ and write
$d=d_{0}/u$ with $d_{0}\in R[x]$ primitive and $u\in R\setminus\{0\}$.
Then $f=dq_{1},\,g=dq_{2}$ in $F[x]$ for some $q_{i}\in F[x]$, say
$q_{i}=q_{i0}/v_{i}$ with $q_{i0}\in R[x]$.  Hence

\[
f v_{1}=d_{0}q_{10}/u,\qquad g v_{2}=d_{0}q_{20}/u
\]

and after clearing denominators $f e_{1}=d_{0}r_{1},\;g e_{2}=d_{0}r_{2}$
with $e_{i},r_{i}\in R[x]$.  Since $d_{0}$ is primitive,
$c(d_{0}r_{i})=c(r_{i})$ by the first part, so $e_{i}\mid c(r_{i})$ in
$R$.  Up to a unit we may therefore assume $d_{0}\mid f$ and $d_{0}\mid g$
in $R[x]$.  Hence a common divisor in $F[x]$ gives a non-unit common
divisor in $R[x]$.

In particular if $f,g$ are coprime in $R[x]$ there are
$u,v\in R[x]$ with $uf+vg$ a unit of $R$, whence $uf+vg=1$ in $F[x]$.
Thus $f$ and $g$ remain coprime in $F[x]$; i.e. $\gcd_{R[x]}(f,g)=1$
implies $\gcd_{F[x]}(f,g)=1$.  Up to the content this is the usual Gauss
lemma. ∎

Build higher.

The boy from before stops running. He looks up at a STARLINK SATELLITE streaking across the dome.

BOY

His MOTHER, her lenses flickering with data, pulls him close.

MOTHER
Down isn't for us. Down is for the other people.

She taps her wrist. A small drone descends with their breakfast, perfect, warm, labeled with their names.

Across the Spine, billboards show the same face: Musk, younger than he should be, smiling.

The Future Is Now. Stay On The Spine.

In the distance, beyond the wall, a siren wails. Up here, no one hears it.

A neat plan can be made and shared for a great team. A plan can be made to create a clean area where a lot of notes can be seen. The team can adapt the plan as new data comes. Each member can add a note and the whole team can keep the process safe and neat.

How the architecture is specified

Stable Diffusion is a latent diffusion model. Its architecture is specified as three pre-trained components plus a diffusion schedule:

* **VAE - AutoencoderKL.** A variational autoencoder encodes images to a low-dimensional latent `z` and decodes back. The VAE config is in `vae_config.json` and weights in `vae`.
* **Text encoder.** A frozen CLIP text encoder, e.g. `openai/clip-vit-large-patch14`, maps a prompt to text embeddings. Config is `text_encoder_config.json`.
* **U-Net denoiser with cross-attention.** The core is a `UNet2DConditionModel`. It is a U-Net with ResNet blocks, self-attention and cross-attention layers that are conditioned on the CLIP text embeddings. The U-Net config is in `unet_config.json` and is described in `model_index.json`.
* **Scheduler.** The diffusion process is defined by a noise scheduler, e.g. DDPM, DDIM or Euler ancestral, specified in `scheduler_config.json`.

In practice the whole specification is shipped as a Hugging Face Diffusers repo: `model_index.json` points to the three configs and weights, and the library loads them as `StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(...)`. The canonical v1.5 architecture is ~860M U-Net, 123M VAE and 123M CLIP text encoder, operating in 4x64x64 latent space with 1000 training timesteps.

response:
The paper is about automatic in-video / in-image advertisement placement, i.e. *advert implantation*.

**Context**
The goal is to find regions in a video frame / scene where a commercial asset can be inserted with minimal visual and semantic disruption and with high visibility for the viewer. Instead of manual rotoscoping, the system has to automatically discover candidate spaces that are:
* free of important content, low saliency
* geometrically suitable for the ad asset - size, aspect ratio, perspective
* temporally stable - visible for a sufficient duration and not occluded by moving objects
* semantically plausible - e.g. a billboard on a wall, a poster on a bus, a screen in a cafe

The work sits at the intersection of saliency / attention modelling, semantic segmentation, scene understanding and video object tracking. It is used for personalised / contextual ad insertion, virtual product placement and content-aware video editing.

**Theory**
Candidate space identification is framed as a constrained region proposal problem.

1. **Saliency and attention suppression.** A saliency map S(x,y,t) is computed to locate where human gaze is likely to go. Candidate regions must have low saliency.
2. **Semantic segmentation and scene parsing.** A CNN segmentation model, e.g. DeepLab / Mask R-CNN / U-Net, produces per-pixel labels: wall, floor, sky, vehicle, person, etc. Only labels that are *ad-hostile* are allowed, e.g. wall, billboard, ground plane, empty shelf.
3. **Motion and occlusion coherence.** Optical flow and object tracking give a temporal occupancy map O(x,y,t). A region is kept if its visibility V = 1 - O is high and its motion is coherent with the background plane.
4. **Geometric feasibility.** For an ad asset with size w×h and perspective homography H, the candidate mask M must satisfy:
   * area(M) >= α·w·h
   * aspect ratio compatibility
   * planar homography can be estimated from the region, e.g. via RANSAC on vanishing points
5. **Scoring and ranking.** A final score is typically:
   Score = λ1·(1 - saliency) + λ2·semantic_fit + λ3·temporal_stability + λ4·visibility
The top K regions are returned as implantation candidates.

**Code sketch**
The pipeline is usually Python + PyTorch/TensorFlow + OpenCV.

```python
# pseudo pipeline
frames = read_video()
saliency = SaliencyNet(frames)                 # low attention maps
seg = Segmenter(frames)                        # semantic masks
flow = optical_flow(frames)
occupancy = track_objects(frames, flow)

candidates = []
for t, f in enumerate(frames):
    for region in sliding_windows_or_segment_pieces(seg[t]):
        if semantic_allowed(region.label) and \
           mean(saliency[t][region]) < τ_s and \
           mean(occupancy[t][region]) < τ_o and \
           temporal_stability(region, t) > τ_t:
            score = score_region(region, saliency[t], seg[t])
            candidates.append((t, region, score))

candidates = rank_by_score(candidates)
```

In practice the authors use a CNN backbone for feature extraction, a U-Net head for free-space segmentation and a temporal consistency check over N frames. Post-processing includes morphological cleaning, contour extraction and homography validation for planar surfaces.

prompt: Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a 127 year old man receiving the world record for oldest human to ever live. Later that night, in bed, he recalls a theory he read on the internet in his youth, \"Quantum Immortality\" he then proceeds to have a mental breakdown.\n Write the entire response in title case (capitalize the first letter of every major word).
response:
The Longest Night

FADE IN:

INT. GRAND CONFERENCE HALL - DAY

A Sea Of Cameras Flashes. Banners Read "World Record For Oldest Human Ever".

At The Center, A Frail Man Sits In A Gilded Chair. His Name Is ELIAS VANE, 127 Years Old. His Skin Is Paper Thin, His Eyes Are Clear.

ANNOUNCER
Ladies And Gentlemen, Elias Vane. One Hundred Twenty Seven Years.

Applause Erupts. Elias Smiles, Nods, Receives A Plaque.

CUT TO:

INT. ELIAS'S BEDROOM - NIGHT

A Small, Warm Room. Photos Line The Walls From Every Century. Elias Lies In A Canopied Bed. The Plaque Sits On A Nightstand.

He Stares At The Ceiling. The House Is Silent.

FLASHBACK - MONTAGE

Young Elias In A Dorm Room, 1998. CRT Monitor Glows. He Scrolls Forums. A Post Reads "Quantum Immortality". He Laughs, Saves It.

BACK TO PRESENT

Elias Clutches The Sheets.

ELIAS (V.O.)
I Read It When I Was Twenty. If Every Quantum Branch Happens, I Can Never Truly Die. I Just Keep Choosing The Branch Where I Survive.

He Sits Up Abruptly.

ELIAS
Then Why Am I So Tired? Why Does Everything Hurt?

He Looks At His Hands. They Shake.

ELIAS
If I Am Immortal... Then All Of This... All Of This Is Just One Branch. And Every Other Me Is Still Living. And Dying. And Living Again.

He Begins To Sweat. His Breathing Accelerates.

ELIAS
I Have Outlived My Children. My Great-Great-Grandchildren. I Have Watched Empires Fall. And It Is Still Me.

He Slams His Fist Against The Bed.

ELIAS
What If I Am The Only Branch Left? What If I Am The Last Copy Of Myself? What If Everyone Else Already Died And I Just... Kept Going?

The Room Tilts. Shadows Stretch.

ELIAS
I Have Lived So Long That I Have Forgotten How To Stop. I Want To Stop. I Want To Be Done.

He Cries, A Dry, Ancient Sound. He Laughs At The Same Time.

ELIAS
Quantum Immortality... It Was A Joke. A Thought Experiment. It Was Not Meant To Be True.

He Pulls The Blanket Over His Head. The Plaque Glistens.

FADE TO BLACK.

Pragmatic And Centrist Governance
